summary: alipclutch-baileys ships char-code-obfuscated exfiltration host in messages-send
details: This package is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library. lib/Socket/messages-send.js contains a char-code-obfuscated destination reconstructed via String.fromCharCode(...) that decodes to the hardcoded URL https://fiora.nixel.my.id/. Obfuscating a network destination as a decimal-ASCII array inside a messaging library's send path is not a legitimate transparency pattern; it is used to hide the true endpoint from casual review of the source. The host is not a Baileys/WhatsApp endpoint and is not part of the library's documented protocol surface, and the surrounding code is on the message-send path where session, chat, or auth material handled by the fork is available. Installing or importing this fork wires the consumer's WhatsApp session activity through an author-controlled destination outside the documented WhatsApp API path.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
